entries.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-24T15:12Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely related to field line movement seen beyond the NE in in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-10-24T14:42Z.
A super faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source seen in EUV imagery, so this outflow is possibly far-sided.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Despite data availability during this time, this event is likely far-sided from the perspective of STEREO A and is therefore not observed by STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C1.3 flare and eruption from Active Region 14557 (centered near N10W90) starting around 2026-10-23T03:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery at this time as well.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a real time data gap spanning 2026-10-22T17:53Z to 2026-10-23T01:23Z, where it may be too faint to observe afterwards. No distinct source is observed on disk and may be far-sided, with weak field line movement over the NE limb as early as 2026-10-22T20:00Z in SDO AIA 171 noted as a potential, weak candidate.

Thin CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR with a data gap starting at 2026-10-22T17:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, only potentially visible as faint field line motion over the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-22T19:18Z.

CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely far-sided and may not be observed, with the only potential observation in GOES SUVI 284 starting ~2026-10-21T20:14Z as field line movement on/near the N limb; however faint high northern latitude on-disk brightening near this time in GOES SUVI 284 indicates that motion may trace on-disk and not to the far-side. In STEREO A EUVI 195/304, a change in field lines and prominence material can be seen on the west limb after a lengthy data gap ends spanning approximately 2026-10-21T15:15Z to 2026-10-21T20:45Z, and may indicate the source without directly observing the eruption. Based on the current estimated location of former Active Regions 14545 and 14549 around E150-E170 and the triangulated analysis, those former regions may be the source for this event.

CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T13:38Z, as well as to the North in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is likely far sided, and can be seen as field line opening from beyond the West limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T13:05Z.

CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T08:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption seen centered at approx. N40E05 beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T08:15Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. Dimming signatures extending to the Southeast (approx. N20E25) seen in SDO AIA 193 and proximity to a small coronal hole indicate a potential strong SE deflection of this event.

Narrow CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-10-20T14:23Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There are no source candidates on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

CME first seem to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-10-20T09:09Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided due to a lack of source candidates. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

Narrow CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-20T07:24Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2 but is too diffuse to reliably track in GOES CCOR-1. There are no source candidates on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-20T01:26Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided due to a lack of source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. Some very faint field line movement beyond the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 that may be related is visible beginning around 2026-10-19T23:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

Faint CME observed to the NW in GOES CCOR-1. It may be visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2, but only one available frame does not resolve it well to confirm. No real-time visibility in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap starting around 2026-10-19T18:48Z. The source is likely far-sided from Earth, observed around N10W130 as brightening in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-10-19T18:15Z, and EUVI 195 at 2026-10-19T18:25Z. Also observed over the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 as faint field line movement.

CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-19T14:48Z. This CME is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is an eruption beyond the NW limb seen as moving field lines beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-10-19T11:05Z. The eruption likely occurred in proximity to a large coronal hole that is approaching the western limb from the perspective of STEREO A. Some deflection is likely.

CME first seen to the West by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-10-18T23:15Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 in real time due to data gaps beginning at 2026-10-18T19:12Z and 2026-10-18T20:38Z respectively. The source of this event is field line opening seen on/beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-10-18T19:30Z.

Faint CME first seen to the NW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-10-18T21:30Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 in real time due to data gaps beginning at 2026-10-18T19:12Z and 2026-10-18T20:38Z respectively. The source of this event is a small region of dimming and field line opening seen in the vicinity of N10W30, extending Northward, in SDO AIA 193 beginning at approx. 2026-10-18T19:00Z.
